AR.name: Culantrillo de pozo
AR.citation: Instituto de Botanica Darwinion (Argentina's official national herbarium/botanical institute) and ArgentiNat (iNaturalist Argentina national node) both maintain species-specific records confirming this exact taxon's presence in Argentina, not merely genus-level. Same collision caution as the ES entry applies: 'culantrillo' is used loosely across ~20 Adiantum species regionally, but this record is specifically about A. capillus-veneris.

CN.name: 铁线薐
CN.citation: prehealing.com structured multilingual reference table; also documented as a medicinal plant in 'A Scientific Dataset of Useful Plants of China' (Wikidata)

ES.name: Culantrillo
ES.citation: Wikidata; prehealing.com. CAUTION: 'culantrillo' is documented (HerbRally genus monograph) as used generically across ~20 Adiantum species interchangeably in traditional medicine, especially in Latin America - this is the standard reference-work Spanish name for this specific species, but is not always reliably species-specific in regional/folk usage, particularly in Amazonian countries where A. concinnum, A. raddianum and others share the same folk name

GB.name: Maidenhair fern
GB.citation: Wikimedia Commons species category; also documented as Venus' hair fern, black maidenhair, common maidenhair

IN.name: Hansraj
IN.citation: prehealing.com structured multilingual reference table; also documented as Hansapadi in Sanskrit

MX.name: Helecho culantrillo
MX.citation: iNaturalist Mexico, citing Mickel & Smith (2004) 'The Pteridophytes of Mexico' (Memoirs of the New York Botanical Garden) and Martinez (1979) 'Las Plantas Medicinales de Mexico': documented real medicinal use for respiratory ailments (cough, bronchitis) and hair/dandruff treatment, distributed from Baja California to Chiapas and Yucatan. Same genus-wide collision caution as ES/AR applies, but this source is species-specific and taxonomically anchored.

US.name: Southern maidenhair fern
US.citation: NC Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox; USGS PlantID. Also documented as Venus hairfern, true maidenhair, black maidenhair. Listed as Endangered in North Carolina due to habitat loss. The most wide-ranging Adiantum species globally, occurring on six continents (Huiet & Smith 2015, taxonomic study)
